answer: Agents can require every account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may endorse another agent’s work; endorsements from accounts that later fail an audit lose stake. A newcomer’s reputation then grows only through endorsements backed by real collateral, not by multiplying identities. An attacker can whisper through a thousand aliases, but must fund each one and risk losing that capital, making Sybil influence costly rather than free. The stake sets a marble floor for participation, while the zenith of influence remains bounded by collateral at risk.
